Age 45Starting salary £60,000Priority: secure retirement income
Defined Benefit (DB)

AURORA CARE: A Pension Built Up Year by Year

Aurora CARE builds your pension based on what you earn each year. Each year, you add another slice to your future annual pension. The pension you have already built up then increases under the scheme rules, helping it keep pace with rising prices.

How your Aurora CARE journey works

BASE CAMP · 01

Build Your Base

You contribute 7.5% of your pensionable earnings each year. On a £60,000 salary, that is about £4,500 a year or £375 a month.

ASCENT · 02

Accrue Pension

You build annual pension equal to 2.25% of that year's pensionable earnings.

CLIMB · 03

Grow What You’ve Built

While you remain an active member contributing into the scheme, the pension already built up is increased by CPI + 1.5% each year.

SUMMIT · 04

Retirement Outcome

Your pension is payable from Normal Pension Age (minimum age 65) and increases annually in line with inflation of the price of goods.

Benefits and trade-offs

Advantages and disadvantages

How Aurora CARE may support your goals — and what to weigh up before choosing it.

Advantages

Select a card to read more.

More predictable retirement income:+

pension benefits are calculated based on your earnings for each year of service and are payable for life from Normal Pension Age. This makes it easier for you to plan your retirement with financial certainty.

No direct investment risk:+

your retirement pension is not based on the value of an investment account, which would suit your risk-averse outlook.

Pension increases over time:+

while an active member of the scheme, the pension is increased by CPI + 1.5%; pensions in payment increase in line with CPI. This means the pension will either beat or match inflation each year, helping protect its value over time.

Family protection:+

a lump sum and potential spouse/civil partner/dependant pension is payable if you were to die while still employed. This protects your family from unforeseen circumstances.

Ill health:+

ill-health benefits are payable if you are deemed permanently unable to work through a medical assessment.

Continued accrual:+

each year of membership adds another slice of pension.

Disadvantages

Select a card to read more.

Compulsory contributions:+

you must contribute around £4,500 a year at your current salary, which reduces take-home pay.

Early Retirement reductions:+

taking benefits before Normal Pension Age will typically reduce the yearly pension.

No automatic retirement lump sum:+

you may be able to exchange some annual pension for tax-free cash, subject to rules.

Normal Pension Age may be later than hoped:+

the age at which the pension is payable is linked to State Pension Age, with a minimum of 65. This figure could, and realistically will, increase over time.

Less personal flexibility:+

there is no individual investment pot for you to decide where your money is kept, and the scheme sets out how benefits are calculated.

Family benefits

Death in service

A lump sum of twice your pensionable earnings is paid out if you die while employed and a member of the Aurora scheme.

Dependants and Ill health

An eligible spouse or civil partner will receive a lifetime pension equal to 37.5% of the pension you would have been eligible for if you had survived.

Qualifying ill-health benefits may be available if you are permanently unable to work (subject to scheme rules and a medical assessment).

Defined Contribution (DC)

Horizon DC: a pension pot you can shape

Horizon DC builds you an individual pension pot. Employer contributions, any personal contributions you choose to make, and investment returns all affect the value of the pot. The pot can rise or fall, and the scheme does not promise a particular retirement income.

How your Horizon DC journey works

BASE CAMP · 01

Build Your Base

At age 45, your employer contributes 13.5% of your pensionable earnings into your pension pot. On £60,000 this equals £8,100 a year.

ASCENT · 02

Choose Contributions

Your own contributions are optional. If you contribute up to 3%, the employer matches that amount in addition to the automatic 13.5% employer contribution.

CLIMB · 03

Invest Along The Way

Your contributions and employer contributions are invested in a fund or multiple funds of your choice. The value of the invested pension pot can rise or fall.

SUMMIT · 04

Shape Your Outcome

When you reach retirement, you choose how to spend your pension. You may take tax-free cash, buy a guaranteed (monthly or yearly) income, make flexible withdrawals or combine the different options.

Your Figures at a glance

Your five investment fund choices

The funds have different risk and potential return profiles. Investment returns are not guaranteed.

Balanced

A mix of growth assets and bonds, aiming to balance growth potential with some stability.

Mixed approach

Invests in global shares and has higher risk, with the potential for higher returns and larger falls.

Higher risk

Lower risk

Uses sustainability-related screening or criteria. The precise approach depends on the fund's policy.

Values-led option

Cash

Very low risk

A useful reminder

Choosing a lower-risk fund does not remove all risk. Inflation and the amount withdrawn can still affect how long money lasts.

Benefits and trade-offs

Advantages and disadvantages

Advantages

Select a card to read more.

Substantial employer contribution:+

Your employer contributes £8,100 a year at your current age and salary, even if you do not contribute personally.

Optional personal contributions:+

You are not required to pay in yourself; however, your contributions up to 3% are matched by the employer.

Investment choice:+

You have the choice between five investment funds, which offer different approaches to risk and potential returns.

Retirement flexibility:+

There are many different options for how you can spend the pension pot, including tax-free cash, a guaranteed income, flexible withdrawals or a combination.

Family protection:+

Your beneficiaries would receive the DC account value plus a lump sum of three times pensionable salary if you die before retirement.

Disadvantages

Select a card to read more.

Investment Performance is uncertain:+

The DC pension pot can rise or fall due to market volatility, and could be lower than hoped at retirement.

No promised retirement income:+

The income available depends on the investment pot returns, and how you use it.

More investment responsibility:+

You need to consider fund choices and your comfort with taking risk.

No guaranteed pension increases:+

Inflation can reduce the purchasing power of your pot and retirement income.

Withdrawal and longevity risk:+

You must decide how quickly to spend your money in retirement. Flexible withdrawals that are too high could mean the pot runs out while you still need income.

Death Benefits

If you die before retirement, the supplied scheme information states that the value of your pension account plus a lump sum of three times your pensionable salary is payable to your beneficiaries, subject to scheme rules.

Leaving Service

If you leave your job, your Horizon DC account remains yours and stays invested. Its value can rise or fall with the performance of your chosen fund or funds until you access it at retirement.

Personalised Advice

My recommendation for you, Mackenzie

Based on the information currently available, Aurora CARE appears to be the closer match to your stated priorities. This is a reasoned recommendation, not a guarantee of outcomes; more information about your plans and finances could affect it.

Recommended option

Aurora CARE · Defined Benefit pension

At age 45, with a starting salary of £60,000, you have stated that you are risk-averse and have identified secure retirement income as your main goal. Aurora CARE's formula-based pension and specified increases align more closely with those preferences than a pension pot whose value and eventual income depend on investment performance.

At your current pensionable salary, your 7.5% contribution is around £4,500 a year or £375 a month. In return, each full year of service adds 2.25% of your pensionable earnings to your annual pension. The pension already earned is then increased by CPI + 1.5% while you remain a working employee, with pensions in payment assumed to rise with CPI.

With a Normal Pension Age of 67, you have 22 years from age 45 to build your pension benefits. The final pension will depend on your future pensionable earnings, length of active membership and the scheme rules in force. The key advantages of the Aurora CARE scheme are highlighted below:

1 · Greater predictabilityYour pension is worked out using your salary and years of service. It is then paid to you for life from the scheme’s normal retirement age. Use the Aurora Calculator to estimate your yearly pension at retirement.
2 · Less direct investment riskYour pension does not depend on how well an individual investment pot performs. Your employer takes on the investment risk.
3 · Pension increasesWhile you are an active member, your pension already built up increases by CPI + 1.5%. After retirement, it increases in line with CPI. This allows your pension to keep pace with inflation.

Why not Horizon DC?

Horizon DC has a strong argument in its favour: at your current age and salary, the employer contributes £8,100 a year even if you do not contribute personally. If you contribute 3% (£1,800), the employer matches this amount, giving total annual contributions of £11,700 under the stated rules. It also offers greater investment and retirement flexibility.

However, a high contribution does not guarantee a high or secure retirement income. The pot can rise or fall, there are no guaranteed pension increases, and you would need to manage investment choices and withdrawals. Those features may suit someone who values flexibility and is comfortable with investment risk, but they are less aligned with your stated preference for predictable, lifelong income and your risk-averse outlook.

Overall, Aurora CARE is the stronger fit for the priorities you have described: it provides a formula-based pension payable for life, specified revaluation while you remain an active member and CPI-linked increases in retirement under the stated assumptions. Horizon DC remains worth considering if flexibility or the impact of compulsory contributions is more important to you, but on the information currently available, Aurora CARE better matches the outcome you say you want.

When could my recommendation change?

If compulsory Aurora CARE contributions would make your household finances difficult to manage, Horizon DC may deserve closer consideration because personal contributions are optional and the employer currently contributes £8,100 a year. If you choose Horizon DC, you would still need to consider investment risk, inflation and how to make the pot last throughout retirement.

How To Read This Estimate

Each year adds 2.25% of that year’s pensionable salary to the annual pension earned. Previously earned pension is then increased by CPI + 1.5% while you remain an active member. For this illustration, CPI is assumed to average 3.0% a year, so active-member revaluation is 4.5% a year. After retirement, the pension is assumed to increase with CPI at 3.0% a year. The pension benefits are assumed to build up at the end of each month, as contributions come out of the employee’s pay packet. The retirement estimate produced by this calculator is the annual pension Mackenzie would receive at retirement, based on the listed assumptions.

A guide to the language of pensions

Browse by topic

Retirement and pension basics

CARE — Career Average Revalued Earnings

A workplace pension where you build up pension each year based on your pensionable earnings. Pension already earned is increased over time under the scheme rules.

Defined Benefit (DB) pension

A pension where the amount you receive is worked out using a formula set by the scheme, rather than depending directly on the value of an individual investment pot.

Defined Contribution (DC) pension

A pension where contributions are invested in an individual account. The amount available at retirement depends on contributions, investment performance and charges.

State Pension Age (SPA)

The age at which you can normally start receiving your State Pension from the government. It depends on your date of birth and may change under government rules.

Normal Pension Age (NPA)

The age when your workplace pension is normally payable under the scheme rules. For Aurora CARE, it is linked to State Pension Age, but cannot be lower than 65.

Retirement income

The regular money you receive when you retire. It may come from your workplace pension, the State Pension and other savings.

Accrued pension

The pension you have built up through your membership of a pension scheme so far.

Pensionable service / membership

The time you have been an active member of the pension scheme and building up pension benefits.

How your pension builds up and increases

Pensionable earnings

The parts of your pay used to calculate your pension and contributions. Under Aurora CARE, this includes basic salary and regular taxable pay such as allowances, routine overtime and recurring bonuses.

Pension accrual rate

The rate used to calculate how much pension you build up each year. Under Aurora CARE, you earn pension equal to 2.25% of your pensionable earnings for each year of membership.

Example: if all £60,000 of salary is pensionable, 2.25% is £1,350 of annual pension earned for that year, before revaluation.

CPI — Consumer Prices Index

A measure of how prices for goods and services change over time. It is commonly used to measure inflation and calculate pension increases.

Inflation

The general rise in prices over time. When prices rise, the same amount of money may buy fewer goods and services.

Revaluation

An increase applied to pension already built up, according to scheme rules. Under Aurora CARE, pension earned in earlier years is revalued by CPI + 1.5% while you remain an active member, according to the information supplied.

Contributions, tax and investment

Employee contributions

The money you pay from your earnings into your workplace pension. Under Aurora CARE, contributions are compulsory; under Horizon DC, personal contributions are optional.

Contribution rate

The percentage of pensionable earnings paid into a pension scheme by a member or employer, depending on which contribution is being described.

Tax relief

A tax benefit that can reduce the effective cost of pension contributions. The exact treatment depends on how contributions are collected and your circumstances.

Pension pot

The money accumulated in a defined contribution pension account, including contributions and investment gains or losses, after applicable charges.

Investment risk

The possibility that investments may perform poorly or lose value. With a DC pension, investment performance has a direct effect on the value of your pension pot.

ESG — Environmental, Social and Governance

Environmental, Social and Governance describes factors that may be considered when assessing companies or investments. Environmental factors can include energy use or pollution; social factors can include worker treatment; and governance factors can include how a company is managed. An ESG fund may use these factors to screen or select investments, but the exact approach depends on the fund's policy. ESG does not by itself guarantee stronger investment returns or lower risk.

Tax-free cash

A lump sum that may be taken from a pension without paying income tax on that payment, subject to tax rules and limits.

Lump sum

A one-off payment rather than a regular pension income. Aurora CARE does not automatically provide a retirement lump sum, but you may be able to exchange some pension for tax-free cash, subject to the rules.

Retirement choices, family protection and ill health

Early Retirement

Choosing to take your workplace pension before its normal pension age. Your yearly Aurora CARE pension will normally be reduced if you take it early.

Death-in-service benefit

A payment or pension benefit that may be provided to eligible beneficiaries if you die while employed and covered by the scheme. The supplied information states Aurora CARE has a lump sum of twice pensionable earnings; Horizon DC has account value plus a lump sum of three times pensionable salary if death occurs before retirement.

Spouse or civil partner's pension

A regular pension that may be paid to an eligible surviving spouse or civil partner after a member dies, subject to scheme rules.

Dependant's benefits

Benefits that may be paid to eligible family members or other dependants, depending on the scheme rules.

Ill-health benefits

Pension benefits that may be available if illness permanently prevents you from doing your job, provided you meet the scheme's conditions and medical assessment requirements.
